title: Sharp Error Bound for Derangement Ratios

problemStatement.formal: \left|\frac{D(n)}{n!} - \frac{1}{e}\right| \leq \frac{1}{(n+1)!},\quad \frac{D(n)}{n!} \to \frac{1}{e},\quad \text{with even partial sums above } \frac{1}{e} \text{ and odd partial sums below it.}
problemStatement.plain: Proves the sharp convergence rate |D(n)/n! - 1/e| ≤ 1/(n+1)! using the alternating series estimation theorem. The ratio D(n)/n! equals the n-th partial sum of the Taylor series for e^{-1}, and the error is bounded by the first omitted term. Also proves D(n)/n! → 1/e and the alternating property: even partial sums overshoot 1/e from above, odd partial sums undershoot from below.
whyMatters: Connects the classical derangement ratio D(n)/n! with the Taylor expansion of e^{-1}.
Records an explicit factorial error bound rather than only the limiting probability 1/e.
Captures the alternating overshoot and undershoot behavior of the partial sums.

# Knowledge Base: derangements-oq-03

Insights accumulated during research on this problem.

---

## Problem Understanding

The local problem statement asks for the sharp convergence rate
`|D(n)/n! - 1/e| <= 1/(n+1)!` for derangements. It frames `D(n)/n!` as the n-th partial sum of the Taylor series for `e^{-1}` and points to the alternating series estimation theorem as the intended proof mechanism.

---

## Insights

- The main mathematical bridge is the equality between the derangement ratio and the finite alternating exponential sum.
- The error bound should follow from bounding an alternating-series remainder by the first omitted term.
- The target includes the parity behavior: even partial sums overshoot `1/e`, while odd partial sums undershoot it.
